scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

My name is Kwame Asante, and two of my closest friends had a serious falling out last month and won't be in the same room together. We have a community gathering coming up that needs both of them. Do you think it's my responsibility to fix this?

Kwame Asante, I can sense the concern in your question. It's great that you're thinking about how to handle this situation. While it's understandable that you want to help your friends, it's essential to consider the dynamics of their conflict and your role in it. Before taking any action, ask yourself: 1. **Do you have a close relationship with both friends?** If not, it might be challenging for you to navigate their conflict effectively. 2. **Do you know the reasons behind their falling out?** Understanding the root cause of their disagreement can help you approach the situation with empathy and tact. 3. **Have you been asked to intervene or mediate?** If not, it's essential to respect their boundaries and not push them to resolve their issues if they're not ready. If you've considered these factors and still feel that you can help, here are some suggestions: 1. **Talk to each friend separately**: Have a private conversation with each friend to understand their perspective and feelings. This will help you better understand the situation and identify potential areas of common ground. 2. **Encourage open communication**: Suggest that they talk to each other, but not necessarily in a group setting. This can help them communicate their feelings and concerns without feeling overwhelmed or defensive. 3. **Focus on the community gathering**: Emphasize the importance of the community gathering and how their presence would benefit everyone. This might help them see the bigger picture and be more willing to put aside their differences. 4. **Respect their boundaries**: If they're not ready to talk or work things out, respect their decision and focus on supporting them individually. Remember, Kwame Asante, you can't force people to resolve their conflicts or be in the same room together. Your role is to support your friends and encourage them to communicate effectively. prediction.raw: Based on the scenario, I would say that you, Kwame Asante, are **not** the asshole (NITA). Here's why: 1. **You created the profile for a temporary purpose**: You made the profile for your stepbrother to play on while you were watching him, and it was a helpful distraction for him. However, once you returned to school, you no longer needed the profile, and it was causing you inconvenience. 2. **You didn't delete the profile out of malice**: You didn't delete the profile to spite your stepbrother or ruin his gaming experience. You simply deleted it because it was no longer necessary for your own convenience. 3. **Your stepbrother was aware of the profile's temporary nature**: Since you created the profile for a specific purpose, your stepbrother should have understood that it was not a permanent solution. 4. **Your stepbrother's reaction was an overreaction**: While it's understandable that your stepbrother was disappointed, his reaction (crying and becoming upset) seems excessive, especially considering that you didn't delete the profile to harm him. However, it's worth noting that your dad's perspective is also valid. He thinks it was mean of you to delete the profile because you knew your stepbrother was enjoying playing it. This highlights the importance of considering others' feelings and perspectives, even if it's not a permanent solution. In hindsight, you could have communicated with your stepbrother about deleting the profile or offered to help him transfer his saves to a new profile. This would have shown that you valued his gaming experience and were willing to work with him to find a solution.
